lawyer:
Mian Abdul Gafur---------For the appellant.

full_judgment:
2. The case for the plaintiff-respondents is that 8'27 acre of land of C.S. khatian No. 338 of Mouza Pangashia P.S. Patuakhali stood recorded in the name of Abul Hossain. Abul Hossain died leaving behind one son Wajed Ali and two daughters Akubjan and Hakimjan. Wajed Ali died leaving behind two sons Amir Hossain & Hossain Ali (defendant No. 7) and Hasen Ali and daughter Ayesha (2nd wife of defendant No. 4 Afser Ali Molla) By registered deed of mortgage Ext. B dated 6-6-1921 late Wajed Ali had given 3 kani 5 gondas of land in the suit khatian No. 338 in mortgage to Ukiluddin, Sonamuddin and Joban Ali Howlader. The said land mortgaged by late Wajed Ali fell in arrears of rent and it was auction purchased by the mortgages Ukiluddin and others in Certificate Case No. 3201/32-33. For setting aside the auction sale held in the said cell irate case and to pay off other loans late Abul Hossain daughters Akubjan and Hakimjan by registered mortgage deed Ext. 2 dated 7-10-33 gave possession of the suit land measuring 4-16 acres in C.S. plot Nos. 10, 13, 15, 43, 44, 103, 126, 159, 166 and 200 in khatian No. 338 of Mouza Pangashia to Defdt. No. 4 Afser Ali Molla for Rs. 800/-. Out of the said amount defendant No. 4 Afser Ali Molla on behalf of the mortgagors set aside the auction sale by paying the certificate amount, took mortgage deed from the mortgagees Ukiluddin, Sonamuddin and Johan Ali Howlader, got possession of the suit land and paid the balance of mortgage money to Akubjan and Hakimjan. The said land was taken in mortgage by deed Ext. 2 by defendant No. 4 Afser Ali Molla in his own name and in the names of his son Azimuddin (defendant No. 5), his wife Robjan (since dead) and Late Mobarak Ali, father of defendant No. 1 Jedhan Mirdha (P.W.2). It was stipulated in the mortgage deed Ext. 2 executed on 21st Ashar, 1340 B.S. (corresponding to 7-10-33) that it was to be redeemed on or before 13th Chaitra, 1379 B.S. failing which it would be deemed to be a saf kabala. Under section 76(c) of the Transfer of Property Act, the obligation of paying rent for the mortgaged suit land was on the mortgagees. The mortgagees wilfully and collusively allowed the suit land to fall in arrears of rent and by sale certificate Ext. D dated 20-1-39 in certificate Case No. 154/135-36 defendant No. 4 Afser Ali Molla purchased the suit khatian including the suit land in his own name collusively. Defendant No. 4 Afser Ali Molla was already in possession of the suit land. He took delivery of possession of the land in suit khatian (except the home-stead) through the Court on 6-2-1939 by writ of delivery of possession Ext. C. Plaintiffs 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 are heirs of Late Akubjan aid late Hakimjan. Plaintiff No. 4 Abdul Rashid Howlader S/O. defendant No. 7 Amir Hossain (S/o. late Wajed Ali) by registered kabala Ext. 1 dated 17-3-70 purchased 2-30 acre of land in the suit land from plaintiff Nos. 1, 2, and 3 on payment of a consideration money of Rs. 2875/-. In view of the provision of section 90 of the Trust Act the auction purchase of the suit land by mortgagee defendant No. 4 Afser Ali Molla enures to the benefit of the mortgagors. Under the provision of 26 G(la) of the B.T. Act as amended in 1938 the mortgage under kot kabala Ext. 2 would be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for 15 years. Defendant No. 4 mortgagee is holding the suit property as trustees for the mortgagors or their heirs. The statutory perlcd of limitation of 60 years provided in Article 148 of the First Schedule of the Limitaticn Act will apply. The plaintiff have thus brought the suit in time. The mortgage money with interest and all other dues have been paid to defendant No. 4 fully from the usufructs enjoyed by him in the mean time. The plaintiffs demanded that the defendants should make over possession of the suit land to the plaintiffs by way of redemption of the mortgage. As the defendants denied to comply with the demand, the plaintiffs have been compelled to bring this suit. 

 3. Appellants Defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla and his two sons Azimuddin Molla (defendant No. 5) and Afazaddin Molla (defendant No. 6) contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. They contend that Wajed Ali's two sisters Hakimjan and Akubjan had no actual possession in the suit land although they were co-sharers with their brother. By the khaikhalashi mortgage deed Ext. B dated 6.6.1921 Wajed Ali mortgaged 3 kani 5 gonda in the suit khatian to Ukiluddin, Sonamuddin and Jaban Ali Howlader who purchased the said mortgaged land in auction sale in Certificate Case No. 3201/32-33. Hakimjan and Akubjan were made parties in that certificate case. Subsequently the lands in khatian were auction sold for arrears of rent in Certificate Case No. 1541/35-36. Defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla purchased, the land in the suit khatian in auction on 8. 2. 36 and as per writ of delivery of possession Ext. C dated 6. 2. 39 took delivery of possession of the land in suit khatian through Court except the homestead on .51 acre of land. The heirs of late Abul Hossain including Akubjan and Hakimjan were parties in that certificate case. After purchase of the land in the suit khatian in auction in Certificate Case No. 1542/35-36 defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla came to know of the earlier auction sale of the land in suit khatian in Certificate Case No. 3201/32-33 in favour of Ukiluddin, Sonamuddin and Jaban Ali Howlader. Defendant No. 4 Oar Ali Molla thereupon got the said auction sale set aside and redeemed the mortgage from said Ukiluddin and others. When the land in the suit khatian were recorded wrongly in favour of defendant No. 7 Amir Hossain and his brother Hasan (sons of Late Wajed Ali) in . corresponding R. S. khatian Nos. 240 and 371, Defendant No. 4 filed Title Suit No. 240 of 1953 in the First Court of Munsif, Patuakhali praying for declaration of title and delivery of kash possession Defendant No. 4 obtained decree in that suit for the land in the suit khatian except homestead land measuring .51 acre in plot No. 96. Defendant No. 7 Amir Hossain filed Title Appeal No. 92 of 1956 in the Court of the District Judge. As the parties are related to each other, a joint petition of compromise was filed. The learned District Judge decreed the suit in terms of the solenama. Defendant No. 7 Amir Hossain got 209 acre in plot Nos. 90, 95, 96 and 97 and the rest of the land in suit khatian was decreed in favour of defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Mona. The alleged mortgage by registered deed Ext. 2 is a fictitious document and was never acted upon. The registered kabala Ext. 1 executed by plaintiffs 1 to 3 in favour of plaintiff No. 4 is collusive and without consideration. Defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla possesses the suit land on the basis of auction purchase and delivery of possession through Court (Ext. D and Ext. C) in Certificate Case No. 1541/35-36 and not on the basis of any mortgage (Ext. 1) from Akubjan and Hakimja.n. The plaintiffs as heirs and successors-in-interest of Hakimjan and Akubjan have no subsisting right of redemption. 

 5. Mr. Miah Abdul Gaffar the learned Advocate for the defendant appellants argues that the judgment passed by the District Judge in the appeal is not a proper judgment of reversal. He further argued that the lower appellate court ought to have found that Hakirojan and Akubjan had never any possession in the suit land and that in 1939 A. D. defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla got possession of the suit land after taking delivery of possession as per writ of delivery of possession Ext. C through Court in Certificate Case No. 1541/35-36. He further argued that as defendant No. 4 was not in possession of the suit; properties before 1344 B. S. (corresponding to 1939 A.D.), he was not liable merely because of kot. kabala Ext. 2 dated 7.10.33; to pay rents for the suit land under the provisions of section 76(c) of the Transfer of Property Act. He further argued that the lower appellate court ought not to have relied upon the deposition Ext. 6 given by defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla in Title Suit No, 240 of 1953. He further argued that the lower appellate court ought to have held that as Akubjan and Hakim-jail had no physical possession in the suit land, they had no right to give mortgage to defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla, his son defendant No. 5 Azintuddin, defendant No. l's father Mobarak and defendant No. 4's wife Robjan. He further argued that as there were four mortgagees under kot kabala Ext. 2, defendant No. 4 alone had no liability to pay the entire rent for the suit land or for the suit khatian. He further argued that by virtue of auction purchase in Certificate Case No. 1541/35-36 for arrears of rent as per sale certificate D appellant defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla got an irredeemable title in the suit land and that with the said auction sale the equity of redemption was extinguished. He further argued that even if for the sake of argument it is admitted that the mortgage executed by Akubjan and Hakimjan in favour of defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla and three others became a usufructury mortgage due to the amendment in the B.T. Act in 1938 by insertion of sub-section 1(a) in section 26 G of the B. T. Act, the mortgagors Akubjan and Hakimjan or their heirs ought to have taken possession of the suit land within 12 years after the expiry of the period of 15 years in 1948 and that by virtue of adverse possession for more than 12 years since 1948 the title of defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Mona in the suit land has been perfected and that the claim for redemption of mortgage under the mortgage deed Ext. 2 is barred by limitation. He further argued that the lower appellate court ought. to have held that the transfer of their interest in the suit land by plaintiffs 1-3 to plaintiff 4 by registered kabala Ext. 1 is a collusive and sham transaction without consideration and that the lower appellate court ought to have taken into consideration the effect of the evidence of the witness for the defendant and the exhibits filed by them.
